bio:
Vancouver-born Chinese-Canadian singer-songwriter Tyler Shaw entered the national pop conversation with "Kiss Goodnight," which became a platinum Canadian single and helped earn him a 2014 JUNO nomination for Breakthrough Artist of the Year. His 2015 debut Yesterday expanded that early momentum with songs including the gold-certified "House of Cards" and "Wicked," establishing Shaw as a durable presence in a Canadian radio-pop landscape increasingly shaped by streaming as well as traditional airplay.

Shaw's second album Intuition produced his biggest sustained radio run. "Cautious" went gold, while "With You" reached double-platinum certification and became the most-played single by a Canadian artist on Canadian radio in 2019. Intuition was nominated for Pop Album of the Year at the JUNOs, and Shaw's touring history broadened through dates with Selena Gomez, Shawn Mendes and Alessia Cara. Rather than relying on one breakout, he built a catalogue of repeated Top 10 Canadian radio singles.

His later work expanded that visibility beyond conventional release cycles. Shaw co-led the ArtistsCAN charity recording of "Lean on Me" with Fefe Dobson during the pandemic, while his "abcdefu Romantic Version," released as "Love You Still," became a large TikTok-driven success and was certified platinum in Canada. Shaw's longevity gives him an important place in 2010s and 2020s Canadian pop, while his visibility as a Chinese-Canadian male pop artist adds another dimension to a mainstream industry in which Asian Canadian representation has historically been limited.
Montréal-born Nigerian-French Canadian singer-songwriter TÖME blends alternative R&B, Afrobeats and pop in a global-facing catalogue that has earned Juno recognition.

Toronto hip-hop group UBAD, also known as Ubad Missive, formed in the 1980s around members Groovy, Rugged, Tyson and Ebony. Their mid-1990s independent catalogue includes The Legacy, Life’s Gettin’ Rough and Rugged & Nasty, placing them among the city’s early generation of recorded rap crews.

Nova Scotia DJ and producer Uncle Fester is a veteran of Canadian hip-hop whose work spans beatmaking, engineering, touring, the Backburner collective and production for artists across the East Coast underground scene.

Unotopic is an Edmonton artist with Canadian and Guatemalan roots whose music sits within the urbano latino space. Born in 2001 and based in Alberta, he blends Latin urban influences with contemporary pop and hip-hop production. Northern Dial carries Unotopic as part of its Western Canadian Latin and urban catalogue.

USS, short for Ubiquitous Synergy Seeker, is a Canadian alternative dance duo formed in Toronto by Ashley Buchholz and Jason 'Human Kebab' Parsons. The group built a national following by combining rock, electronic production, turntablism and high-energy live performance. Northern Dial carries USS as part of its modern Canadian alternative catalogue.

Halifax rapper, songwriter, producer and composer Vadell Gabriel has spent more than a decade developing a style he calls Nerd Jack Swing, mixing new jack swing, boom-bap, chiptune and R&B. Raised between Halifax and Dartmouth, he is also active in Atlantic Canadian music through the Pyrate Radio project and soundtrack work for animation and games.
Montréal group VALAIRE makes groove-heavy electronic music shaped by jazz, funk and hip-hop, evolving from the band's earlier Misteur Valaire name.

Vandalizm is a Canadian R&B and hip-hop collaborator active in Toronto's contemporary independent scene. The artist has released music with Toronto R&B singer Sage Harris, including 'Raw,' 'Poseidon' and 'No Falling,' and appears in Canadian and Toronto-focused R&B discovery contexts alongside that work. Northern Dial carries Vandalizm as part of its current Toronto-area R&B and hip-hop catalogue.

vbnd is a Saskatoon, Saskatchewan bassist, producer and recording artist whose music blends jazz, funk, neo-soul and alternative R&B. Signed to UK label DeepMatter, he built his catalogue through releases including Daughter of the Sun and Scum Funk, often working with the Saskatoon musicians who became The Soulmate Collective. Ten vbnd tracks from those projects and related singles appear in the Northern Dial library.

Vermeil is an emerging indie-pop artist from Quebec City whose French-language music pairs intimate writing with grainy synths, subtle electronic textures and a melancholy pop sensibility. Her catalogue includes songs such as L'œil, Remède, Sommeil and si je ne suis pas, the latter appearing in the Northern Dial library.

Canadian singer-songwriter VIBI developed a pop sound around a raspy, powerful vocal tone and diaristic songwriting, later relocating to Los Angeles while maintaining her Canadian identity. Her work combines singer-songwriter intimacy with polished Scandinavian-influenced pop production, allowing her to move between stripped emotional writing and larger, hook-driven arrangements.

Mentorship connected to the Stargate production world helped sharpen that pop vocabulary, while the Rain In California project earned placement on Spotify and Amazon Music editorial playlists. VIBI also opened for Bryan Adams before a crowd of roughly 60,000 and won the pop category grand prize in the John Lennon Songwriting Contest, giving her independent career notable performance and songwriting milestones beyond streaming alone.

Her subsequent catalogue has expanded quickly through releases including Mattress, we had fun, didn’t we?, "homesafe," "killshot" and the 2026 EP angeldies. VIBI’s strongest through-line is emotional specificity: even as the production grows more polished, the songs remain centred on vulnerable, conversational writing rather than anonymous pop architecture.
Abbotsford-born singer, songwriter, dancer and actor Victoria Duffield is a Canadian pop artist best known for the platinum-certified dance-pop single Shut Up and Dance.
Toronto-born and raised singer-songwriter Victoria Staff makes Canadian indie pop built around intimate storytelling, folk-leaning melodies and candid writing about relationships and mental health.

Victory is a Calgary hip-hop and R&B artist whose melodic approach blends rap with contemporary R&B. Coverage of his early releases identifies him directly with Calgary's emerging music scene. Northern Dial carries Victory as part of its contemporary Alberta hip-hop catalogue.

Vilaxxs is a Canadian multi-genre electronic artist whose music spans dark ambient, jumpstyle and phonk. Also associated with the names SERAPHIX and Zyrek, the project is known for atmospheric production built around deep pads, plucked melodies and nostalgic textures. Northern Dial carries Vilaxxs as part of its contemporary Canadian electronic catalogue.

Vince 'Vinny Mac' Maria is a Canadian producer, songwriter and musician whose career developed through Toronto's dance and remix scene. A five-time Juno nominee, he has produced and remixed work for Canadian and international artists and is a member of the Canadian dance project Hellbent. The Ryder Remix of Hellbent's Fast Car is his Northern Dial library credit.

Montreal singer-songwriter and multi-disciplinary artist Vincent Khouni is the leader of garage-rock band Double Date with Death and also records solo material. His solo work moves between alternative pop, psychedelic rock and electronic textures, with releases including 8:12pm and Accident and appearances at Coup de coeur francophone and Les Francouvertes.

Virginia to Vegas is the pop project of Derik John Baker, who was raised between the United States and Ontario before establishing himself in Toronto's songwriting scene. After online demos brought him to the attention of Wax Records, he signed with the label in 2013 and broke through with "We Are Stars," a collaboration with Alyssa Reid that introduced his melodic electronic-pop approach to Canadian radio. The early success led to a Canadian Radio Music Awards breakthrough honour and set up his first full-length album, Utopian.

Rather than disappearing after that initial single, Baker built Virginia to Vegas into a consistent radio act. Songs including "Lights Out," "Selfish," "Just Friends" and "betterman" became Top 10 and multi-platinum Canadian hits, while a JUNO nomination reflected his growing place in the domestic pop landscape. The 2020 project Don't Wake Me, I'm Dreaming continued his preference for clean electronic production, emotionally direct melodies and songwriting designed to work equally well on radio and streaming playlists.

A period working in Los Angeles broadened Baker's international writing network, but he later returned to Toronto and built a more self-contained creative team around the project. That move reinforced what makes Virginia to Vegas notable in Canadian pop: the act is not defined by celebrity persona so much as repeatable songcraft. Across more than a decade, Baker has turned understated electronic-pop writing into a catalogue of Canadian radio staples and one of the steadier homegrown pop careers of the streaming era.
Vancouver-born Barbadian-Canadian singer-songwriter Vita Chambers makes pop-rock and electropop, building an independent career after early major-label releases and touring with Justin Bieber.

VLXL is a Toronto hip-hop duo formed by Via Linez and Lyve. Their music draws on classic boom-bap while incorporating contemporary production, and their album Trains, Automobiles and Flights features Canadian collaborators including Tanika Charles, Junia-T and Tona. Northern Dial carries VLXL as part of its Toronto independent hip-hop catalogue.

VT is a Montreal rapper associated with Saint-Leonard whose music sits within Quebec's contemporary street-rap scene. His French-language catalogue reflects Montreal's francophone hip-hop culture and the city's newer independent rap movement. Northern Dial carries VT as part of its Montreal hip-hop catalogue.

Formed in Burlington, Ontario, Walk Off the Earth spent years developing a highly visual, multi-instrumental approach before a 2012 cover of Gotye's "Somebody That I Used to Know" transformed the band's reach. The video, built around five musicians playing a single guitar, became a viral phenomenon and demonstrated the group's central idea: arrangements and performance concepts could be as important to online discovery as the song itself. The attention led to a major-label deal and gave the band an international audience without requiring it to abandon the do-it-yourself video culture that created the breakthrough.

Walk Off the Earth converted that attention into an original catalogue. R.E.V.O. included the Canadian hit "Red Hands," while Sing It All Away helped the group win the 2016 JUNO for Group of the Year. The band maintained a heavy international touring schedule and continued treating unconventional instruments, tightly coordinated videos and pop songwriting as parts of the same creative language. After the death of keyboardist and vocalist Mike "Beard Guy" Taylor in 2018, the group honoured him publicly and continued recording and performing.

Later projects broadened the band's audience further, including the children's Romeo Eats series, whose second volume won a JUNO, and the 2023 single "My Stupid Heart." Walk Off the Earth's significance is closely tied to a particular shift in Canadian music culture: they were among the acts that showed how a band could use YouTube-era visual invention to build a global audience, then turn viral attention into a sustained recording and touring career.

Toronto rapper Wave Montega emerged from Malton with a style shaped by the multicultural environment of the city’s west end and by the Jamaican music he heard growing up. A published poet from childhood, he began releasing music in 2018 after time in the United States on a basketball scholarship. His early breakout "Side Bag" helped establish a local audience and led into the 2020 project Still Wavy.

Montega’s 2022 album Catharsis widened the sound beyond straightforward rap, moving among drill, grime, R&B and dancehall while keeping his writing focused on depression, relationships, betrayal and loss. That flexibility reflects both Toronto’s genre-crossing rap culture and Montega’s own Caribbean background. Later releases continued the pattern, including METHADONE and 2026 material that kept his catalogue moving between hard-edged street rap and more introspective songs.

His importance in Northern Dial’s contemporary catalogue comes from that refusal to flatten Toronto rap into one sound. Montega’s work connects Malton, Jamaican-Canadian musical memory, UK drill influence and modern independent rap in a way that feels specific to the city rather than generically international.
Québec City rapper Webster, born Aly Ndiaye, is a Canadian hip-hop artist, educator and historian whose French-language work is closely tied to Black history and Québec culture.
Cape Breton fiddler, pianist and step dancer Wendy MacIsaac is a Canadian traditional musician whose work carries forward Nova Scotia's Gaelic and Cape Breton music traditions.

Western Motel is a Vancouver indie band whose catalogue moves between lo-fi pop, folk and guitar-driven alternative music. The group emerged in 2021 with releases including Kensington Park Tapes and a self-titled album, later returning with Months Between Transmissions and the 2026 Badass Dragon EP.
Toronto-born, Vancouver Island-based producer and DJ WHIPPED CREAM, born Caroline Cecil, makes bass-heavy electronic music spanning trap, house and festival-oriented club production.
Montréal rapper White-B, born David Bouchard-Sasseville, is a Canadian francophone hip-hop artist and member of the 5sang14 collective known for melodic street rap.
Toronto rapper Why G is a Canadian hip-hop artist from the city's west end whose elastic delivery and menacing production became part of Toronto's modern street-rap sound.

Wide Mouth Mason formed in Saskatoon in 1995 around guitarist and singer Shaun Verreault, bassist Earl Pereira and drummer Safwan Javed. The trio built its identity on blues and soul vocabulary played with the force of a contemporary rock band, and its early live reputation centred on Verreault's elastic singing, improvisational guitar work and the group's unusually tight rhythm section. After the independently released The Nazarene attracted major-label attention, Warner Music Canada issued the band's 1997 self-titled album, which brought songs including "Midnight Rain," "My Old Self" and "This Mourning" to Canadian rock radio and earned the group a JUNO nomination for Best New Group.

The 1999 album Where I Started became another major step, earning gold certification in Canada and widening the band's sound without abandoning its blues foundation. Stew followed in 2000 and brought another JUNO nomination, this time for Best Rock Album. Wide Mouth Mason's reach also came through the road: the band toured with acts including The Rolling Stones, AC/DC and ZZ Top and performed at the Montreux Jazz Festival, placing a Saskatoon power trio inside a much larger international blues-rock tradition.

Wide Mouth Mason continued well beyond its late-1990s breakthrough rather than settling into catalogue-act status. Pereira eventually left the group, while Verreault and Javed kept recording with collaborators including Big Sugar's Gordie Johnson. I Wanna Go With You in 2019 explored a leaner roots-blues approach, and Late Night Walking in 2023 paired the band with producer Ryan Dahle while again featuring Johnson on bass. That longevity matters: Wide Mouth Mason is one of the clearest links between prairie blues-rock, the Canadian alternative-radio era and a continuing culture of musicianship-first touring bands.

Canadian husband-and-wife duo Wild Strawberries, formed by Roberta Carter-Harrison and Ken Harrison, makes moody, introspective pop-rock and alternative music through a long-running independent catalogue.
Toronto recording artist and producer William Dinero, born William Grajeda, makes hip-hop, R&B, Latin and crossover production alongside soundtrack work for film and television.

William Prince grew up on Peguis First Nation in Manitoba, where music first functioned less as entertainment than as service. His father was a preacher and musician, and Prince learned to accompany him on guitar while travelling to First Nations communities and singing at church services, wakes and funerals. That background shaped the measured pace, deep baritone and sense of emotional responsibility that became central to his songwriting. His debut album Earthly Days introduced that voice nationally and won the 2017 JUNO for Contemporary Roots Album of the Year, turning a regional Manitoba singer-songwriter into one of Canada's most distinctive new roots artists.

Prince expanded that foundation rather than abandoning it. Reliever developed his folk-country writing on a broader production scale, while the 2020 companion project Gospel First Nation returned directly to the hymns, communities and contradictions of the Christian tradition in which he was raised. Stand in the Joy continued the arc in 2023 with songs built around love, family and survival rather than treating Indigenous identity as a fixed subject category. Across that catalogue, Prince has earned two JUNO Awards, received the John Prine Songwriter Fellowship and appeared on stages ranging from NPR's Tiny Desk to the Newport Folk Festival, building an international audience without separating his work from Peguis and the Manitoba Interlake.

His fifth album, Further From the Country, arrived in October 2025 and widened the sonic frame with a more expansive band while returning to questions of distance, grief, identity and what it means to leave home without severing it. The record's title captures the tension running through Prince's career: his music has travelled far beyond the community where he learned to play, but its power still comes from the restraint, storytelling and communal purpose formed there. In Canadian roots music, Prince represents a contemporary Indigenous songwriting voice that can sit naturally beside country, gospel, folk and Americana traditions while remaining unmistakably grounded in his own place and experience.
Nova Scotia band Wintersleep makes expansive Canadian indie rock that combines atmospheric guitars, rhythmic experimentation and melodic songwriting across a catalogue dating to the early 2000s.

Malvern emcee Wio-K is a veteran Canadian hip-hop artist whose laid-back patois-tinged flow appeared on the landmark Rap Essentials compilation, Kardinal Offishall's Ol' Time Killin' and recordings with the Monolith crew.

Toronto-based Ethiopian-Eritrean artist Witch Prophet, born Etmet Musa, blends experimental R&B, soul, jazz, hip-hop and electronic music with layered vocals and self-produced, identity-driven songwriting.

Wizdome Bunitall, also known as DJ Bunitall, is Canadian DJ, producer and music-industry veteran Joshua Barclay. Active since the early 2000s, he has worked across promotion, A&R, DJing and production while remaining tied to Toronto's underground hip-hop scene. His full-length collaborations with Asun Eastwood include Let Me Talk My Sh*t and Let Me Talk My Sh*t Too; his production and artist credit on Toro 4's featuring JD Era is the Northern Dial library entry.
Mi'kmaq rapper and producer Wolf Castle is a New Brunswick artist whose energetic hip-hop mixes sharp bars, self-produced beats and Indigenous perspective.

Wolfy Lights is the electronic and drum-and-bass project of Sherry St. Germain, a classically trained multi-instrumentalist, producer, singer and songwriter with Toronto roots. St. Germain has also worked under the AKYLLA name and has collaborated with artists across electronic, hip-hop, film and television music. Bombalaya, its Blooom remix and Born Again are the three Wolfy Lights tracks in the Northern Dial library.

Toronto-born, Brampton-raised producer, songwriter and record executive WondaGurl is one of Canada's most influential contemporary hip-hop producers, with credits for Jay-Z, Travis Scott, Rihanna and Drake.

Halifax-born, Toronto-based rapper Wordburglar, born Sean Jordan, makes upbeat alternative hip-hop built around dense wordplay, humour, pop-culture references and his work with the Backburner collective.

X2FromTheCIV is a hip-hop artist active in Toronto's independent music community. His catalogue includes State of Mind and Heavily Humbled, along with recurring collaborations with Toronto-based artist and engineer Sam-r, HXGO, Tadiie and other members of the surrounding scene. Northern Dial carries X2FromTheCIV as part of its contemporary Toronto hip-hop catalogue.

Xentury is a Toronto hip-hop and R&B artist whose independent catalogue connects her with the city's rap and soul community. She has recorded across the Greater Toronto Area with artists including Dan-e-o, Michie Mee and DJ Mercilless while developing her own releases and XI Entertainment. Her appearance with Masta Ace on Dan-e-o's 2024 single Cleanse My Soul is her Northern Dial library credit.

Xpress aka DJXP is a Canadian-born DJ and producer of Nigerian and Jamaican heritage based in Toronto. The brother and longtime musical collaborator of EverythingOShauN, he works across hip-hop, R&B, Afro and pop as a producer, songwriter and DJ, with credits extending from Canadian independent music to television and film placements.

Scarborough-born Canadian-Tamil producer, songwriter, engineer and mridangist Yanchan Produced blends Carnatic percussion and South Asian musical traditions with hip-hop, R&B and electronic production.

YessirXD is a Montréal rapper and melodic hip-hop artist whose releases include Bad Habits, Mama Don't Worry, Pave The Way and Scars. His music blends contemporary rap with melody-driven songwriting, and he has collaborated with artists in Canada and the United Kingdom. His feature on CHINO WAWA's 2025 track FLAWS from Glue ll is his Northern Dial library credit.

Toronto-born R&B singer, songwriter and producer Yoko Gold, born Moses Peterson, first emerged through solo releases before gaining wider attention through collaborations with his brother Tory Lanez. His atmospheric contemporary R&B catalogue includes the independent project Escape From Limbo and singles such as Limbo, Mirage and Obsolete.

Young Don Million is a Toronto-area hip-hop artist associated with the Jane and Finch scene. The artist appears with Young Smugglaz on 'Sam Taylor' from the 2024 compilation 'Jane & Finch Most Wanted, Vol. 1,' tying the project directly to one of Toronto's longstanding rap communities. Northern Dial carries Young Don Million as part of its Jane and Finch and Toronto hip-hop catalogue.
